text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- Black market trade in cameras and photographic equipment hits profits of producers and legitimate sellers in Poland.
- Poland's small TUK insurer, specialising in transport insurance, plans to increase capital to 30 million zlotys in 1997 from the current 10 million and introduce new products.

- The Supreme Doctors' Council has demanded that Health Minister Jacek Zochowski resign over allegations that he had failed to address the problem of trade in debts of hospitals which made illegitimate purchases of medical equipment.
- Clothes maker Cora Garwolin has launched a 10 million zloty commercial paper programme to boost production.

- The Polish Chamber of Commerce forecasts Poland's gross domestic product at 6.6 percent in 1997 and year-on-year inflation at 13.4 percent in December, against the government's targets of 5.5 percent and 13 percent respectively. It sees nominal wages growth at 18.5 percent .

- According to a report by the London-based Economic Policy Research Centre, food prices in Poland would jump by between 40 and 50 percent after it joined the European Union and some heavy industries would collapse. But Poland, which would pay some $4 billion annually in premiums to the EU, would get about $11.3 billon a year in subsidies from Brussels.
- The Bank Handlowy brokerage recommends Krakchemia shares as "buy" in a recent report.
